ordered.title: The misconception that costs owners time

blocks.text: "Rebuilding my engine is cheaper than replacing it."
Rebuild and replacement costs are often comparable . The difference is downtime and matching-numbers preservation .

Key distinction: Rebuild = you send your engine away. It's stripped, machined, rebuilt, and returned to you. Your car is off-road for 1-3 weeks . Replacement = you buy a ready-to-fit exchange unit. Your car is off-road for 3-7 days . The rebuild process is longer because: engine removal, strip-down, inspection, parts ordering, machining (cylinder boring, head skimming, crank regrind), reassembly, and testing all add time. [EM-OBSERVED]

"In the UK engine industry, rebuild and replacement costs are often comparable. The primary differentiator is downtime tolerance and matching-numbers value. Rebuild preserves your original block - replacement gives you a different engine, faster."
